title: Graph-Augmented Learning to Rank for Large-Scale Knowledge Graphs
summary: This community centers on the paper 'Graph-augmented Learning to Rank for Querying Large-scale Knowledge Graph,' published at AACL/IJCNLP 2022. The work addresses the challenge of querying large-scale knowledge graphs by integrating graph structures into learning-to-rank methodologies. It represents a specific technical contribution within the broader field of knowledge graph reasoning and retrieval.
key_findings: The paper was published in the Proceedings of the 2nd Conference of the Asia-Pacific Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics and the 12th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (AACL/IJCNLP 2022).
The publication appeared in Volume 1: Long Papers, specifically on pages 82–92, during the online-only event held from November 20-23, 2022.
The research was conducted by a team of six authors: Hanning Gao, Lingfei Wu, Po Hu, Zhihua Wei, Fangli Xu, and Bo Long.
The work is cited in the context of 'Towards Foundation Models for Knowledge Graph Reasoning,' indicating its relevance to advanced KG reasoning tasks.
The paper focuses on 'Graph-augmented Learning to Rank,' suggesting a methodological approach that leverages graph topology to improve ranking performance for queries.
It is positioned alongside other recent works in knowledge graph question answering and retrieval-augmented generation, such as those by Yifu Gao et al. (2024) and Yunfan Gao et al. (2024).
